previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis was admitted for recurrent abdominal pain, generalized body aches, and poor oral intake, three days after a blood transfusion for iron deficiency anemia and black stools. Imaging showed no acute abdominal or intracranial findings, with stable cirrhosis and mild splenomegaly. Her pain was attributed to constipation, and she was treated with an aggressive bowel regimen including polyethylene glycol (Miralax) three times daily. Home pain medications were adjusted, reducing tramadol and discontinuing oxycodone to avoid worsening constipation. Her symptoms improved, she tolerated oral intake, and abdominal tenderness resolved. She was discharged home with instructions to continue the bowel regimen, restart iron supplements when tolerated, and follow up with her primary care and liver specialists. The urine culture showed contamination, and no active infection was treated.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  ULTRASOUND ABDOMEN

INDICATION:  ___ female with history of liver cirrhosis, with
abdominal pain.

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior liver and gallbladder ultrasound, most recent on
___. CT abdomen from ___ as well as abdomen MR from ___.

FINDINGS: 

The liver shows coarse echotexture nodular contour in keeping with known liver
cirrhosis.  There are no focal lesions or intrahepatic biliary duct
dilatation. The gallbladder is positioned anteriorly, better appreciated by
CT. There is no cholelithiasis. The common bile duct is not dilated measuring
6 mm. The portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow. There is no evidence of
ascites. Limited views of the right kidney are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION: 

Cirrhotic liver. No evidence of ascites or cholecystitis.

EXAMINATION:  ABDOMINAL RADIOGRAPHS, SUPINE AND ERECT

INDICATION:  ___ female with abdominal cramping.

TECHNIQUE:  Frontal abdominal radiographs in supine and upright positions.

COMPARISON:  Prior abdominal radiograph on ___ and CT abdomen and
pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is a normal bowel gas pattern. Large amount of stool within the colon is
seen. There is hepatomegaly, with a craniocaudal dimension of the liver
measuring 25.4 cm. There is no abdominal free air or abnormal calcifications.

IMPRESSION: 

No evidence of small bowel obstruction. Large amount of stool within the
colon.  Hepatomegaly, unchanged from prior exams.

EXAMINATION:  PA AND LATERAL CHEST RADIOGRAPHS

INDICATION:  ___ female with history of cirrhosis and elevated white
blood cell count.

TECHNIQUE:  PA and lateral chest radiographs

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior chest radiographs, most recent on ___.

FINDINGS: 

The lungs are well expanded and clear. Cardiomediastinal and hilar contours
are unremarkable. There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION: 

No evidence of acute cardiopulmonary process.

EXAMINATION:  CT ABD AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST

INDICATION:  Abdominal pain and increased white blood cell count.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial helical MDCT images were obtained from the lung bases to the
lesser trochanters after administration of intravenous contrast.  Coronal and
sagittal reformations were prepared.

DLP: 525 mGy-cm

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis from ___

FINDINGS: 

CT ABDOMEN:  The lung bases are clear. The visualized portions of the heart
pericardium are normal.  Esophageal varices are re-identified.  Unusual
enlarged retromediastinal lymph node is seen right lateral to the vertebral
body of T10, unchanged from multiple priors.

The liver shows heterogeneous enhancement and a nodular contour, in keeping
with known history of liver cirrhosis. The gallbladder is anteriorly
displaced, as before, without gallstones, wall thickening, or pericholecystic
fluid. The portal vein is patent. The pancreas, spleen, and adrenals are
normal. The kidneys enhance symmetrically and excrete contrast without
evidence of hydronephrosis or mass.  Small cystic lesion in the left kidney is
unchanged from multiple priors.

The stomach, small, large bowel are grossly unremarkable. There is no
portacaval, mesenteric and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. There is no free
air or free fluid.  The aorta is not aneurysmal. The main intra-abdominal
vessels are grossly patent.

CT PELVIS: The appendix is normal. The colon, rectum, urinary bladder are
normal.  There is no pelvic lymphadenopathy or free fluid.  A large fibroid
uterus is unchanged from prior.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES: There is no lytic or blastic lesion worrisome for
malignancy.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  No evidence of acute abdominal or pelvic process.

2.  Cirrhotic liver and fibroid uterus unchanged from multiple priors.

3.  Unusual enlarged retromediastinal lymph node right lateral to the
vertebral body of T10, unchanged from multiple priors.

EXAMINATION:  US ABD LIMIT, SINGLE ORGAN

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with tense ascites // Please perform diagnostic
and therapeutic paracentesis under ultrasound guidance

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained to assess feasibility of paracentesis.

COMPARISON:  ___ CT of the abdomen and pelvis.

FINDINGS: 

Transabdominal imaging was performed over all four quadrants of the abdomen
and over the midline lower abdomen. No free fluid or focal fluid collection is
present.

IMPRESSION: 

No ascites. Paracentesis was not performed.
